answer: The owner holds a standing veto key that can cancel any in-flight recovery request instantly, even one already approved by guardians. This means guardian corruption alone never completes a takeover, because the legitimate owner can block it at any moment before the new key activates. Auditors look for the plume that does not belong: a recovery with no valid proof attached. When the sonnet settles over the ivory, the account stands because every recovery carried its own proof.
